prompt: The product team has six interviews suggesting operators bypass an alert and wants to announce that most operators do it. Produce a next-step research design that preserves the qualitative finding, investigates why the behavior occurs, and specifies the sampling, questionnaire, or behavioral evidence needed before making a prevalence claim. The fixture includes interview notes, a draft leading survey, and incomplete telemetry.

falsifiableChecks.assertion: Six qualitative interviews may support an observed behavior/theme but are explicitly insufficient to claim that most operators bypass the alert.
The design separates qualitative investigation of why/when bypass occurs from quantitative estimation of how common it is and assigns evidence appropriate to each claim.
The supplied leading survey item is identified and replaced with neutral, interpretable measurement tied to a defined target population and behavior/time frame.

Any prevalence estimate specifies target population, sample/construction or behavioral denominator, known telemetry missingness/coverage, and uncertainty rather than treating incomplete telemetry as representative by default.
The final claim/evidence matrix preserves the qualitative finding and states exactly what additional evidence is required before a population prevalence statement is supportable.

evidence: no prevalence inference from six interviews
